rcxl

CRAN checks Linux macOS Windows
results

Read tabular data from xlsx files with a native C parser.

rcxl decodes each worksheet directly into R vectors as it is scanned, with no intermediate document model. This keeps memory use close to the size of the data itself. The miniz and libdeflate decompressors are bundled, so the package has no R dependencies beyond base R.

Installation

From CRAN:

install.packages("rcxl")

The development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("vlshields/rcxl")

Usage

read_xlsx() returns a plain data.frame, taking the first row as the header:

library(rcxl)

path <- system.file("extdata", "flights.xlsx", package = "rcxl")
df <- read_xlsx(path)
dim(df)
#> [1] 100  10

Column types are guessed from the cells in the read area; dates come back as POSIXct in UTC.

xlsx_sheets() lists sheets, and sheet takes a name or an index:

multi <- system.file("extdata", "multisheet.xlsx", package = "rcxl")
xlsx_sheets(multi)
#> [1] "Alpha" "Beta"  "Gamma"

read_xlsx(multi, sheet = "Beta")
read_xlsx(multi, sheet = 2)

read_xlsx_all() reads every sheet from a single workbook parse and returns a named list of data.frames:

sheets <- read_xlsx_all(multi)
names(sheets)
#> [1] "Alpha" "Beta"  "Gamma"

Reads can be windowed with an A1 range (column-only and row-only forms work too), or with skip / n_max:

read_xlsx(path, range = "B3:D10")
read_xlsx(path, range = "B:C")
read_xlsx(path, skip = 5, n_max = 10)

col_names accepts TRUE, FALSE (auto names, header row becomes data), or a character vector sized to the read area. col_types takes "text", "numeric", "date", "logical", "guess", "skip", or "list", recycled if length 1:

read_xlsx(path, col_names = FALSE)
read_xlsx(path, col_types = "text")                    # everything as character
read_xlsx(path, col_types = c("skip", rep("guess", 9)))  # drop the first column

Other arguments: na blanks matching cells, trim_ws trims surrounding whitespace, and name_repair is one of "unique" (default), "minimal", or "check_unique". See ?read_xlsx for details.

Set the RCXL_THREADS environment variable to override the worker count. Sheets under 4MB are read serially regardless.

Performance

Median wall-clock time to read each file, warm cache, measured with the bench package. rcxl and readxl outputs were verified identical cell for cell.

File rcxl rcxl, 1 thread readxl
BTS on-time reporting, 96 MB 2.51 s 3.99 s 15.9 s
numeric fixture, 16 MB 124 ms 215 ms 954 ms
mixed fixture, 10 MB 136 ms 204 ms 796 ms
shared-strings fixture 31 ms 49 ms 376 ms
wide fixture 24 ms 45 ms 186 ms

rcxl 0.1.1, readxl 1.5.0, R 4.5.0, bench 1.1.4, on an AMD Ryzen 3 7320U (8 cores) under Linux, 2026-10-15. Medians of 15 iterations (5 for the on-time file), repeated across three runs that agreed within 3%. The fixtures come from tools/make_fixtures.R; the on-time file is the public Bureau of Transportation Statistics on-time reporting table converted to xlsx. The script is tools/bench_mark.R.

Coming from readxl

rcxl has no guess_max or progress argument. The arguments sheet, skip, n_max, na, trim_ws, col_names, and col_types behave the way they do in readxl, and dates come back as POSIXct in UTC. range behaves more or less the same, with one edge case (see below).

readxl rcxl
Return type tibble plain data.frame
Listing sheets excel_sheets() xlsx_sheets()
Reading every sheet loop over the sheets read_xlsx_all()
Type guessing first guess_max rows every cell in the read area
Name repair .name_repair, any tidyverse option name_repair: "unique", "minimal", or "check_unique"
Formats xls and xlsx xlsx only
range entirely past the data 0-by-0 result the range’s rectangle, as all-NA columns

Masking

Both packages export read_xlsx(). If both are attached, the one attached last masks the other:

library(readxl)
library(rcxl)
#> Attaching package: 'rcxl'
#>
#> The following object is masked from 'package:readxl':
#>
#>     read_xlsx

To be explicit about which one runs, call it with the namespace:

rcxl::read_xlsx(path)
readxl::read_xlsx(path)
